Package hadur117.core.melee

Class MinimumRiskMovement

java.lang.Object
hadur117.core.melee.MinimumRiskMovement
public class MinimumRiskMovement extends Object
Melee movement: minimum risk (MMOVE-1..4), the HawkOnFire and Diamond shape.

Each tick CANDIDATES points on a ring around Hadur are scored and the least risky becomes the destination; the current destination is kept until a point SWITCH_GAIN safer turns up or it is reached. The ring is capped at NEAREST_FRACTION of the distance to the nearest opponent, so Hadur never runs into anyone. Risk is in units of one full-energy opponent 100 px away, the sum of:

  • each opponent's energy (relative to Hadur's) over distance squared, doubled where Hadur would be that opponent's closest robot and half again for an opponent that hit Hadur in the last RECENT_HIT_TICKS ticks (MMOVE-2), and higher for points that run straight at or away from it rather than across it;
  • the virtual bullets: a head-on and a linear aim for every shot an energy drop showed, scored where they would be when Hadur gets to the point (MMOVE-3);
  • a pull off the middle of the field, a push off the walls' last few pixels, Hadur's recent positions, and a fixed per-round noise field, so the path is no pattern;
  • the melee strategy's posture (MMOVE-5).

On a team (T1) each living teammate whose position is fresh adds a term that rises with the inverse square of its distance from the point, taken where the teammate is predicted to be when Hadur gets there, and a term for a path that crosses its predicted track (MMOVE-6, MMOVE-7); the ring is capped by the nearest such teammate as by the nearest opponent; and each member's noise field and opening spot are shifted by its place in the roster (MMOVE-8), so five copies of this function do not choose one destination. Off a team none of this applies and the scoring is what it was.

For the first OPENING_TICKS ticks the closest-robot term doubles again and a pull heads for the nearest wall-adjacent spot away from the corners. With two opponents left the ring shrinks and the lateral weight rises (MMOVE-4), so the movement already orbits when the duel takes over. Everything is deterministic: the noise is a hash.

    • MELEE_SURF

      public static final boolean MELEE_SURF
      MMOVE-15 (arm msurf), the melee surfer: off a team, the top three's way. Each seen shot is a wave weighed by who else is nearer its shooter (crowdWeight(hadur117.core.world.EnemyShot, java.awt.geom.Point2D.Double, java.util.List<hadur117.core.world.EnemyInfo>)); once Hadur's log of that shooter's hits holds TeamDanger.MIN_SAMPLES, its bullets are the learned aims (MMOVE-10's log, fed off a team by Hadur's own hits) in place of head-on and linear; and the destination is chosen by the wave check (TMODE-11): the WAVE_RERANK least risky candidates driven to, scored by risk and the waves' damage on the way. On from 3.21 (pc-melee-surf: +0.99 +- 0.19 census APS, PR #462).
      See Also:
      • Constant Field Values

    • MELEE_DAMAGE_MEMORY

      public static final boolean MELEE_DAMAGE_MEMORY
      MMOVE-22 (arm mdmg), inspired by Diamond's melee movement: off a team, each opponent's risk term weighs by the damage its bullets have done to Hadur over the whole battle, plus DAMAGE_BASE, times its mean distance from Hadur (a gun that hits from afar is the more dangerous), the weights scaled to average 1 over the living opponents. Without it a hit is remembered for RECENT_HIT_TICKS ticks only. On from 3.21: pc-melee-dia dm +0.43 ± 0.17 with the low end +0.26, endgame wins +0.7, others outlived +0.5, skips +8% (PR #503).

With nearest (TMODE-20 OWN) a shot whose source was nearer a teammate than Hadur makes no bullets (MMOVE-9's rule); with only (TMODE-21 HEADON, TMODE-22 LINEAR) each shot makes one virtual bullet, on that aim, at TeamRisk.ONE_AIM_WEIGHT: the team's code aims no other way.     • clip

      Point2D.Double clip(Point2D.Double p)

    • waveBest

      Point2D.Double waveBest(List<Point2D.Double> candidates, MinimumRiskMovement.View v)
      TMODE-11, Ogi's wave check: the WAVE_RERANK lowest-risk candidates, and the destination held if not reached, are each driven to for WAVE_TICKS ticks, and every shot in flight that crosses Hadur's box on the way counts the share of it aimed there. A shot is a profile that sums to its aimed-at weight, not a certain bullet: its virtual bullets' headings share 1 - WAVE_UNIFORM of it, and the rest is spread over its escape angle. The score is risk / median(risk) + 3 x damage / max(0.1, median(damage)), each risk measured from the least of them (the posture term can make risks negative), times SWITCH_GAIN for the held destination.

    • dodgeBest

      Point2D.Double dodgeBest(List<Point2D.Double> candidates, MinimumRiskMovement.View v, List<MinimumRiskMovement.Wave> waves)
      TMODE-27, Ogi's dodge: the TeamDodge.RERANK lowest-risk candidates, and the destination held if not reached, are each driven to through the shot profiles waves for WAVE_TICKS ticks and through the teammates' bullets for TeamRisk.PATH_TICKS; scored as waveScores(double[], double[]), the held destination times SWITCH_GAIN.

    • rerankBest

      Point2D.Double rerankBest(List<Point2D.Double> candidates, MinimumRiskMovement.View v, int rerank, List<MinimumRiskMovement.Wave> waves, List<VirtualBullet> mateBullets, boolean ownFire)
      TMODE-11, TMODE-27: the rerank lowest-risk candidates, and the destination held if not reached, each driven to through the waves for WAVE_TICKS ticks and through the teammates' bullets for TeamRisk.PATH_TICKS; scored as waveScores(double[], double[]), the held destination times SWITCH_GAIN. With ownFire the teammates' bullets add TeamRisk.PATH_K times their damage to the risk, as PATH scores them, instead of joining the waves' damage.
